html:
The Ohrid Literary School was a centre of Slavic learning founded at Ohrid, on the lake in southwest North Macedonia, in 886 by Saint Clement of Ohrid, a disciple of Saints Cyril and Methodius.

Driven out of Moravia, the disciples were welcomed by Boris I of the Bulgarian state, who sent Clement to Ohrid. Clement is said to have taught thousands of pupils, trained Slavic priests and written sermons and lives of saints. He worked with the Glagolitic alphabet while the Preslav school favoured Cyrillic. His monastery of Saint Panteleimon at Plaošnik became a seat of learning. The school made Ohrid one of the main sources of Slavic Orthodox culture; Bulgarians and Macedonians both claim its heritage.
sum: The Ohrid Literary School was a centre of Slavic learning founded at Ohrid, on the lake in southwest North Macedonia, in 886 by Saint Clement of Ohrid, a disciple of Saints Cyril and Methodius.
